title: Research (no κ claim): reorder, re-frame and re-ranking ceilings on the #4610 productive-helper word
body:
**No κ claim.** These are screening ceilings on Cao Yifan's #4610 round-three productive-helper word, which the current #5413 caller still uses. They show where the remaining headroom is *not*.

| Lever | Result |
|---|---|
| Productive re-ranking (finish rank-4/7/8 helpers as rank 9) | always loses (strict subadditivity of x^(1−C)) |
| Longer controllers and query thinning | already closed by #4658/#4659/#4664/#4666/#4674 |
| One climb per register; free reorder | ceilings 0.00715 and 0.00711 (not reachable) |
| Reorder within the exact commutation poset, dimension-only | 0.00331 / 0.00323, but does not lift to real subspaces (332 clashes) |
| **Reorder within the poset + re-frame, exact subspace LP (3.03M variables)** | **≤ 1.17 cost units per local, κ ≤ ≈ 0.003107** |
| Exact subspace MIP, restricted and medium domains | **the current word is optimal (gap 0)** |
| Non-commuting swaps with exact correction ADDs | 0 gains |

**Why.** Each register climbs in 3–9 steps because a scalar ADD needs both operands at the identical frame. The helper frames forced in every valid reordering already cost 3458.82 of 3464.74. Further gains need a redesigned helper factorization, not reordering. Together with #5462 (the owned-relation optimum), this maps the edits on this word that are exhausted.

Everything is in `research/frontier-word-reorder-ceilings/`: README, R12/R13 notes, a working digest of the accounting, tools, logs and solutions. Most bounds are floating-point screens; the README labels which are exact. The positive control `realize.py` rebuilds the current word exactly and passes both native interpreters on all 632 columns.
